title: [DECISION] PBKDF2 restriction forbids ikm_fd (passwords never stored as KEY fds)
description: src/cdev/crypto2dev_fd.c lines 1778-1783: PBKDF2 ikm_fd must be -1 (rejected with -EINVAL if set). This enforces the security principle that passwords are never stored in KEY fds; they are sensitive and must arrive only via write(). HKDF allows ikm_fd (IKM can be derived key material from a prior KDF stage). This asymmetry is non-obvious and security-critical. A password stored persistently in a KEY fd would be held longer than necessary. The restriction is documented inline: 'PBKDF2 IKM must come from write() — passwords are sensitive and are never stored in KEY fds.' This prevents a class of mistakes where a password becomes reusable if mistakenly stored as a symmetric key.
